prompt: This watercolor illustration depicts a bustling theatre backstage area. On the left, a tall man in a velvet coat stands holding a clipboard, his posture rigid and alert. Next to him sits a worn wooden crate, its paint chipped and faded from years of use. In the center, a woman with curly hair points urgently toward a hanging rope pulley system that dangles from the ceiling beams. Beside her, a young boy in oversized boots looks at the pulley with wide-eyed curiosity, his hands clasped tightly behind his back. To the right, an elderly stagehand with grey stubble hands a rolled-up script to a dancer in a pink tutu, who accepts it with a graceful nod. The dancer sits on a metal folding chair, her legs crossed elegantly despite the chaotic surroundings. Behind them, a large mirror reflects the scene, capturing the backs of the performers and adding depth to the cramped space. A black cat sleeps peacefully on top of a stack of costume boxes near the mirror, completely undisturbed by the activity. Near the entrance, a bright red fire extinguisher hangs on the wall, its color vibrant against the muted tones of the brickwork. Finally, a discarded paper cup lies on the floor near the crate, slightly crushed underfoot. There is no digital equipment visible in this analog setting. There is no audience present in this private moment.
